market_pulse.note: Closed down 859.71 points, or 1.67%, at 50,748.46 on Tuesday, according to preliminary Reuters figures, its second straight drop of more than 1% (The Standard/Reuters).

Closed down 75.96 points, or 1.02%, at 7,341.23 in preliminary figures; CoinDesk noted the S&P 500 and Dow were testing their 200-day moving averages late in the session (The Standard/Reuters; CoinDesk).
Closed down 180.42 points, or 0.74%, at 24,329.34 in preliminary figures, a smaller loss than earlier in the day when it was down about 1.5% (The Standard/Reuters; CoinDesk).
December WTI rose 0.3% to settle at $86.01 a barrel, and January Brent gained 0.8% to $93.14, as Gulf tanker attacks offset forecasts of a growing supply surplus (Rigzone).

themes.title: Stocks fall for a second day
themes.summary: All three major indexes ended lower, with the Dow losing about 860 points; one strategist said every S&P 500 sector was down, with software, airlines and banks among the weakest (The Standard/Reuters).

themes.title: Nvidia beats after the close
themes.summary: Nvidia reported record quarterly revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier, and forecast about $130 billion for next quarter; shares rose about 2% to 3% after hours (Nvidia via GlobeNewswire; CoinDesk; Coinpaper).

themes.title: Software stocks slide
themes.summary: Salesforce fell 9.6%, Intuit 7.1% and ServiceNow 6.8%, among the day's biggest decliners; Microsoft fell about 2.4% (24/7 Wall St.; Trading Economics).

themes.title: Markets price a December rate hike
themes.summary: Reuters said markets price about a 95% chance of a quarter-point Fed rate increase in December, after St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem called for hikes sooner (MarketScreener/Reuters; Yahoo Finance).

themes.title: Mixed economic data
themes.summary: October retail sales rose 0.2%, slightly above expectations, while the NAHB homebuilder index fell to 25, its lowest since April 2012 (Yahoo Finance).

sectors.name: Software
sectors.note: Among the clearest underperformers, with Salesforce, Workday, Intuit and Adobe all lower; Salesforce closed down 9.6% (The Standard/Reuters; 24/7 Wall St.).

sectors.name: Financials
sectors.note: Banks lagged; JPMorgan fell about 2.6% after naming a new CFO to succeed Jeremy Barnum in early 2027, and Goldman Sachs fell about 1.8% (The Standard/Reuters; Trading Economics).

sectors.name: Health Care
sectors.note: Led early losses, down 0.9% in the morning as UnitedHealth and Humana each fell 4.7% (MarketScreener/Reuters).

sectors.name: Semiconductors and AI Hardware
sectors.note: A relative bright spot: Arm rose 4.0%, Coherent 3.1% and Broadcom about 2.5%, while Nvidia slipped less than 1% before its results (24/7 Wall St.; Trading Economics).

watch_list.why: Minutes from the Fed's latest policy meeting are due Wednesday, with markets pricing a near-certain December rate increase (MarketScreener/Reuters; The Standard/Reuters).

Anthropic kept its $70–$78 range; final pricing is expected Wednesday ahead of a Nasdaq debut on Nov. 19, with reports it could price at or above the top of the range (MarketScreener/Reuters; CoinDesk).
Nvidia's after-hours gain follows a sharp monthly decline; Wednesday's session will show whether the beat steadies tech stocks near their 200-day averages (CoinDesk; Coinpaper).
